findings.statement: REQ-VER-013 checks only HEAD elements with blocking:true and resolved_as:decision; unknowns[] is not compared with base, and ci does not recompute gate verdicts. An impl-PR can delete a base blocking UNKNOWN, flip it to blocking:false or close it as fact (record written via shell), lifting WAIT without the maintainer.
findings.recommendation: With a new APPROVED, require every blocking id of the base record to stay blocking on HEAD and be closed by a verified decision; name the error and add a scenario.

findings.statement: Detail pull_request compares only <N> from the ref URL. Issue comment ids are repo-global, so ref .../pull/7#issuecomment-3 pointing at a comment on PR 5 passes.
findings.recommendation: Require the PR of the comment returned by the forge to equal <N> (detail pull_request); add a scenario.

findings.statement: The human-only hint covers every policy path outside src/tests/openspec/changes, i.e. all of .warrant/**, including the own record, waivers, evidence and runs that the CLI writes. An agent editing the record gets 'maintainer in factory-change' instead of warrant unknown/transition.
findings.recommendation: Exclude CLI-written Change state and waivers from the hint (or name the CLI command there); add a scenario for .warrant/changes/<change>.json.

findings.statement: SCN-ENF-038 expects the 'previous hint warrant run finish' for a deny under an active Run, but neither delta nor main REQ-ENF-004 text names the hints of that deny.
findings.recommendation: State in the REQ text the hints of an active-Run deny (run finish, run start).

findings.statement: The proposal says a blocking UNKNOWN without a decision with ref is 'not closed'; REQ-KRN-035 says an element is closed when resolution is non-empty, so open_blocking excludes it.
findings.recommendation: Reword the proposal: closed, but the gate FAILs with DECISION_WITHOUT_REF.

findings.statement: REQ-KRN-035 says a blocking UNKNOWN closes only with --ref to a maintainer comment containing the id. It does not say the command checks only the http(s) form and leaves author and text to warrant ci, as REQ-KRN-028 does for its ref.
findings.recommendation: Add: resolve checks the ref form only; author, text and PR are verified by warrant ci (REQ-VER-013).

findings.statement: REQ-VER-011 (not modified) keeps a closed list of REF_NOT_VERIFIED reasons and says an unavailable forge gives exit code 3. REQ-VER-013 adds reason decision and makes forge failure a finding in non-APPROVED PRs.
findings.recommendation: Modify REQ-VER-011 or state the exception explicitly in both places.

findings.statement: UNK ids allocated in records on parallel branches can collide. id renumber covers only openspec/changes/<name>/** and tests, not records, and the text check would accept a comment about the other Change's id.
findings.recommendation: State the collision behavior (finding, renumber of the record) or record it as accepted residual risk.

findings.statement: BASE_BEHIND_UPSTREAM does not say what happens when an upstream is configured but gone, or when git fails while the upstream is resolved.
findings.recommendation: State skip or a named error for an unresolvable upstream.

assumptions.statement: Guard judges shell commands only by check prefixes, so an agent can write the record through shell under guard (REQ-ENF-004).
The RECORD_MISMATCH rules of REQ-VER-011 do not cover unknowns[].

decisions_required.question: Should warrant ci compare unknowns[] of an impl-PR with the base record (removal, blocking flip, closure without decision)?
options: No, accepted residual risk recorded in ADR-0040
